content_voiceover: This is the AQUILA trial, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in twenty twenty four, that led to F-D-A approval of subcutaneous daratumumab for high risk smoldering multiple myeloma. Three hundred ninety adults with high risk smoldering disease were randomized to daratumumab monotherapy or active monitoring. High risk was defined as ten percent or more clonal bone marrow plasma cells plus at least one of the following, a serum M protein of thirty grams per liter or higher, IgA smoldering myeloma, immunoparesis with reduced levels of two uninvolved immunoglobulin isotypes, a free light chain ratio of eight up to one hundred, or bone marrow plasma cells between fifty and sixty percent. Daratumumab was given subcutaneously at eighteen hundred milligrams weekly for two cycles, then every two weeks for four cycles, then monthly for up to thirty nine cycles or thirty six months. The result was a striking reduction in progression, with a hazard ratio of zero point four nine and a P value under zero point zero zero one, translating into sixty three percent versus forty one percent progression free survival at five years.
keypoints: AQUILA trial: daratumumab monotherapy vs active monitoring in high-risk smoldering myeloma, n=390
High risk defined by BM plasma cells 10% or more plus one added factor: M protein, IgA subtype, immunoparesis, FLC ratio, or plasma cell burden
Subcutaneous daratumumab 1800 mg weekly then biweekly then monthly, up to 36 months
PFS significantly improved: hazard ratio 0.49, P less than 0.001
Led to FDA approval of daratumumab for high-risk smoldering myeloma, an early intervention strategy
keypoint_voiceover: For boards, know that daratumumab monotherapy is now F-D-A approved for high risk smoldering myeloma based on the AQUILA trial, showing a hazard ratio of zero point four nine for progression or death. High risk criteria combine at least ten percent bone marrow plasma cells with one added risk factor like a high M protein, IgA subtype, immunoparesis, an elevated free light chain ratio, or plasma cell burden approaching diagnostic myeloma thresholds. This represents a shift toward early intervention in smoldering disease.
